Behold the love, the generous love
Hark, how his sounding bowels move
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 35:12–14, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

12They repay me evil for good, to the bereavement of my soul. 13Yet when they were ill, I put on sackcloth; I humbled myself with fasting, but my prayers returned unanswered. 14I paced about as for my friend or brother; I was bowed down with grief, like one mourning for his mother. PSALM 35:12–14 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 35
When they are sick his soul complains, And seems to feel the smart; The spirit of the gospel reigns, And melts his pious heart. STANZA II
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 2. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
